review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definitions it depends on: logPhase, logPhase_norm, logPhase_add_frequency, profileMode, tripleCoefficient. I grepped the repo for uses of logPhase_norm and logPhase_neg_argument. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about simp behaviour that I observed. The file declares no simp attributes of its own. The only simp-interface issues I found are the unregistered norm lemma and the parallel hand-written reflection-style rewrite lemmas. I checked the other lemmas and `simp only` calls for loops and competing rules and found none.

findings.declaration: pureProfileMode_norm (use of FourierBridge.logPhase_norm as an explicit simp argument)
findings.problem: `FourierBridge.logPhase_norm : ‖logPhase t y‖ = 1` is the canonical normal form for the modulus of a unit phase, but it has no `@[simp]` attribute. Every norm computation has to pass it by hand. Here `simp` needs it as an explicit argument. The repo mentions `logPhase_norm` at about 77 sites across 56 files, usually as a manual `simp only [..., norm_mul, logPhase_norm, mul_one]`. Examples are KernelSeparation `kernelCoordinateWeight_norm`, InverseRawCompact `childLogTest_norm`, TupleWeights, and TwistedProfiles `cases negative <;> simp [FourierBridge.logPhase_norm]`. Because default `simp` does not know the rule, a norm goal containing logPhase factors is not simplified automatically.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `FourierBridge.logPhase_norm` (LocalProductAssembly.lean, line 182) as `@[simp]`. The statement `‖logPhase t y‖ = 1` is unconditional, its left side is a head-symbol pattern, and its right side is the literal `1`. It cannot loop and does not conflict with any other rule. Then `pureProfileMode_norm` can be `by simp [pureProfileMode, norm_prod]`, and the other call sites can drop the explicit argument. Also consider `@[simp]` on `pureProfileMode_norm` itself. It is a unit-modulus fact with a `1` right side. It would let norm goals about `pureProfileMode` close without unfolding the definition.
findings.benefit: Norm goals for products of phases normalize to `1` with plain `simp`. This removes the repeated boilerplate `logPhase_norm` arguments across the DirichletL files and makes the simp set for phase moduli canonical.

findings.excerpt: lemma logPhase_scaled_coordinate (t a y : ℝ) : logPhase t (a*y) = logPhase (a*t) y := by
findings.problem: The phase rewrite lemmas have no shared simp interface. `logPhase_scaled_coordinate` is a local lemma that moves a scalar from the argument to the frequency. The special case a = -1, `logPhase t (-s) = logPhase (-t) s`, is proved separately as `logPhase_neg_argument` in two other files (TwistedProfiles.lean:227 and GaussianSlots.lean:28), each with the same unfold/congr/push_cast/ring proof. `logPhase_add_frequency` lives in FrequencyTwists and is not simp. This file then uses these lemmas via `simp only [profileHeight, logPhase_add_frequency, logPhase_scaled_coordinate]`. Because the lemmas are neither centrally placed nor tagged, each file re-derives and hand-lists its own rewrite set, and the competing orientations (`a*y` moved to the frequency here, a negation moved to the frequency elsewhere) are not reconciled.
findings.proposed_change: Move `logPhase_scaled_coordinate` next to `logPhase_add_frequency` in FrequencyTwists (or into the FourierBridge namespace). Derive `logPhase_neg_argument` from it with a = -1 and `neg_one_mul`, so there is one canonical rewrite. State a single orientation (scalar into the frequency). Optionally state the `mul_comm` variant, with the scalar moved into the argument, separately, so that call sites need not duplicate proofs. Keep both unsimped, or make the shared lemma `@[simp]` only after checking that the `logPhase t (a*y)` rewrite terminates. It does terminate, since the argument shrinks structurally.
findings.benefit: One canonical, documented phase-scaling rule replaces three near-duplicate lemmas, so later files can call one name. The simp-set choices are made in one place instead of per file.
